summary.name: Risograph Printing. Category: Printmaking and Craft Materials. Provenance is explicit in the source.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicitly riso-printed: two or three inks on natural paper, with overprints creating additional tones. Controlled grain, dots, and slight registration offsets are added without sacrificing text. Color separations may be revealed, and printed forms may be swapped.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to posters and illustrations where two-ink overprint is the identity. Hybrids are suggested when typography carries the message or illustrated subjects need a consistent drawing grammar. Event promos and explainers are inferred from suggested combinations, not stated as core uses.
summary.limitations: Only two independent inks (blue foreground, coral accent) plus paper are allowed. Overprint is the sole third tone, so no third ink or gradients. Coral is decorative only at 3.24:1 on paper, so body text stays blue. Grain textures fills, never text. Two-color checks do not verify text over textures or video.
summary.palette: Suggested, not approved: paper #F4EBD8, blue ink #254687 (foreground), coral ink #D95664 (accent_1). Task-supplied exact colors override these and must not be recolored. Blue on paper is 7.69:1, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target. Coral on paper is 3.242:1, failing it. Gradients are disabled. Validate with chroma.js and recheck composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Registration errors stay stable rather than jittering each frame. Ink-plate reveals and printed-form swaps define the look. Motion should be smooth where it helps, while deliberate cuts and reading holds are preserved. Video runs on seekable composition time; hover and scroll apply only to interactive delivery. Patterns motion-012 and motion-015 are optional and need scene support.
summary.audio: The source gives no explicit audio requirement, so audio is unspecified. Options include music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen for topic, audience, and reading holds. Sound accents must not compete with narration, and speech must stay intelligible. No audio assets are supplied.
summary.assetRequirements: Source assets and exact copy are unspecified placeholders. Ink separations, fixed grain, and registration offsets require preprocessing: Pillow in Python for cropping, compositing, masks, and textures, or Sharp in Node.js only, never in the browser. Load local fonts and assets before rendering, and seed any randomness.
summary.combinations: Risograph alone suits posters and illustrations. Suggested hybrid with style-093 for event promos and title cards: headline words reveal as blue, then coral plates. Suggested hybrid with style-028 for explainers: flat figures separate into two plates. Supporting styles must collapse into the two inks and drop their own palettes.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default composition and export pipeline. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. SVG is the style renderer, Pillow prepares ink separations, GSAP drives the seekable timeline, and Motion is optional if synchronized. Verify opening, action, transition, and closing frames, plus the full decoded video.
